changes.before: lower returns the first value ≥key; upper returns the first value >key. Their difference counts matches, and [lower,upper) is the duplicate range. Both searches use the same sorted input but differ in which equality case moves the left boundary. A missing key produces equal boundaries.
changes.after: lower returns the index of the first element whose value is at least key; upper returns the index of the first element whose value is greater than key. Either index may be n when no such element exists. The difference between these indices counts matches, and [lower,upper) is their half-open index range. Both searches use the same sorted input but differ in which equality case moves the left boundary. A missing key produces equal boundaries.
changes.reason: Distinguish returned indices from element values.

changes.before: With a suitable distribution and bounded load, expected lookup and insertion can be O(1). A set of colliding keys can require Θ(n) probes for one operation; resizing also costs Θ(n) occasionally. The fixture constructs a collision cluster and counts occupied positions before the first empty slot to expose the mechanism.
changes.after: With a suitable distribution and bounded load, expected lookup and insertion can be O(1). A set of colliding keys can require Θ(n) probes for one operation; resizing also costs Θ(n) occasionally. The fixture constructs a collision cluster. Its probe counter counts every inspected slot, including the empty slot that ends an unsuccessful search.
changes.reason: Make the stated counting unit agree with absent_probes=4 (three live slots plus one empty slot).

changes.reason: Use the initializer actually shown in the worked example.
